title: Multimodal machine learning prioritizes candidate inhibitors of giant cancer cells
summary: A multimodal ensemble combining chemical fingerprints, drug-induced cell morphology, transcriptomic perturbation profiles and biological annotations was trained on screening data from four breast cancer cell lines, reaching mean Pearson correlation 0.403 and recovering 27.9% of experimentally identified hits in held-out screening data. The model ranked 21,367 compounds from an external library for testing; six candidates preferentially suppressed polyploid giant cancer cells in at least three paclitaxel-treated cell lines, and AZD-8055 and voxtalisib reduced their abundance by at least 70% in all four. Evidence is limited to cell lines and modest predictive accuracy, selectivity against normal cells was not read, and the preprint is not peer reviewed.
ai_technology: Multimodal machine-learning ensemble over chemical fingerprints, cell-morphology and transcriptomic perturbation features ranks compounds for suppressing polyploid giant cancer cells.
organization: UPMC Hillman Cancer Center, University of Pittsburgh; Carnegie Mellon University

evidence.tested: Held-out screening-data hit recovery for the model, then laboratory testing of prioritized compounds in four paclitaxel-treated breast cancer cell lines.
evidence.unknown: Modest predictive accuracy; cell-line readout only; assay design, selectivity against normal cells and in vivo efficacy not reviewed; not peer reviewed.
